_comment: Provenance and tier for every corpus fixture. A fixture with no entry here
tier 'synthetic' — machine-rendered from a known string. Proves the harness
computes CER and that an engine reads Greek at all. MUST NOT back an accuracy
claim: the render has no scan noise, no historical typeface, no skew, and its
ground truth is the input string rather than a human transcription.
tier 'scan' — a real page image with a human diplomatic transcription.
The only tier accuracy baselines may be computed from. Requires 'source',

modern-1.note: Modern sans-serif. Out of domain for the committed Kraken models, which are trained on 19c Porson/German-serif print.

polytonic-1.note: Committed Tesseract baseline is CER 0.0 — a font round-trip, not a recognition result.

byzantine-1.note: Named 'byzantine' but rendered in Arial — no Byzantine typeface, no ligatures. Does not exercise what the name implies.

polytonic-scan-1.source: Τα Βυζαντινά Μνημεία της Θεσσαλονίκης (Πολυχρονιάδης/Δεδούσης), PDF page index 20, printed p. 21, 300 DPI
polytonic-scan-1.licence: © rights holder, used by permission of the rights holder
polytonic-scan-1.transcribed_by: AI-drafted, reviewed and approved by the repository owner
polytonic-scan-1.note: Body prose. First scan-tier fixture in the corpus — the accuracy gates may compute baselines from this tier, unlike the Arial renders above.
